options.text: One, because nitrogen always has a lone pair.
Two, because nitrate has extra electrons.
Zero, because nitrogen forms four bonds in a resonance structure.
Three, because each oxygen donates one.

questions.explanation: In nitrate, nitrogen forms four bonds (one double, two single in a resonance structure) with no lone pairs. Formal charge is +1 on N.
questions.hint: Nitrogen has no lone pairs in nitrate.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.stem: An architect's brief labels Na2O as covalent; what is wrong?

options.text: Nothing; Na2O is covalent.
Na2O is a molecule because it has a formula.
Na2O is metallic because Na is a metal.
Na2O is ionic because Na is a metal and O is a nonmetal.

questions.explanation: Na2O is ionic because sodium is a metal and oxygen is a nonmetal. The covalent label is wrong.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Explain why metals have high melting points
questions.stem: An architect's brief asks why metals have high melting points; what is the reason?

options.text: Because the electron sea strongly binds positive ions.
Because covalent bonds are strong.
Because ionic bonds are strong.
Because hydrogen bonds link atoms.

questions.explanation: The delocalized electron sea strongly attracts positive metal ions, giving metals high melting points. Bonding strength varies with metal.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topic: Valence electrons in the delocalized sea
questions.stem: An architect's brief examines zinc metal; how many valence electrons per atom enter the delocalized sea?
questions.explanation: Zinc, a transition metal, contributes two valence electrons to the delocalized sea. Group 12 metals typically contribute two.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Explain why mercury is liquid at room temperature
questions.stem: An architect's brief asks why mercury is liquid at room temperature; what is the reason?

options.text: Because it has no delocalized electrons.
Because it is ionic.
Because weak metallic bonding allows atoms to move freely.
Because it forms covalent bonds.

questions.explanation: Mercury's metallic bonding is relatively weak, allowing atoms to move freely and making it liquid at room temperature. Bonding strength varies.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topic: Boiling points across a dispersion series
questions.learningObjective: Predict boiling point from molecular weight
questions.stem: An architect's brief compares F2 and Cl2; which has the higher boiling point?

options.text: F2, because smaller molecules boil higher.
Neither, because halogens are gases.
Both equal, because both are halogens.
Cl2, because larger size strengthens dispersion.

questions.explanation: Cl2 is larger with stronger dispersion forces, giving it a higher boiling point than F2. Size increases boiling point.
